translations.chinese: 太史公讀春秋歷譜諜，至周厲王，未嘗不廢書而嘆也。
translations.literal: The Grand Historian read the Spring and Autumn Annals, the chronological tables, and the secret records, but whenever he reached King Li of Zhou, he could not help but set down his book and sigh.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Historian, reading through the Spring and Autumn Annals, the chronological tables, and the secret records, would always lay down his book and sigh whenever he reached the reign of King Li of Zhou.

translations.literal: He said: 'Alas, Master Zhi foresaw it!'
translations.idiomatic: He said: 'Alas, Master Zhi foresaw it!'

context.previous: 太史公讀春秋歷譜諜，至周厲王，未嘗不廢書而嘆也。

translations.literal: When Zhou made ivory chopsticks, Jizi sighed.
translations.idiomatic: When King Zhou fashioned ivory chopsticks, the Viscount of Ji sighed in dismay.

context.next: 周道缺，詩人本之衽席，關雎作。

translations.chinese: 周道缺，詩人本之衽席，關雎作。
translations.literal: When the Zhou way declined, poets based themselves on the bedchamber, and 'Guan Ju' was composed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou way declined, poets based themselves on the bedchamber, and 'Guan Ju' was composed.

translations.literal: When benevolence and righteousness decayed, 'Lu Ming' criticized it.
translations.idiomatic: When benevolence and righteousness decayed, 'Lu Ming' criticized it.

context.previous: 周道缺，詩人本之衽席，關雎作。
context.next: 及至厲王，以惡聞其過，公卿懼誅而禍作，厲王遂奔于彘，亂自京師始，而共和行政焉。

translations.chinese: 及至厲王，以惡聞其過，公卿懼誅而禍作，厲王遂奔于彘，亂自京師始，而共和行政焉。
translations.literal: When it came to King Li, because he hated to hear of his faults, the ministers feared execution and disaster arose. King Li fled to Zhi, and disorder began in the capital. The Gonghe administered government.
translations.idiomatic: When it came to King Li, his hatred of hearing his own faults made the ministers fear execution, leading to disaster. King Li fled to Zhi, and chaos began in the capital itself, leading to the Gonghe administration.

context.next: 是後或力政，彊乘弱，興師不請天子。

translations.chinese: 是後或力政，彊乘弱，興師不請天子。
translations.literal: After this, some ruled by force, the strong oppressed the weak, they raised armies without asking the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: After this, some ruled through force, the strong bullied the weak, and they raised armies without seeking the Son of Heaven's approval.

context.previous: 及至厲王，以惡聞其過，公卿懼誅而禍作，厲王遂奔于彘，亂自京師始，而共和行政焉。
context.next: 然挾王室之義，以討伐為會盟主，政由五伯，諸侯恣行，淫侈不軌，賊臣篡子滋起矣。

translations.chinese: 然挾王室之義，以討伐為會盟主，政由五伯，諸侯恣行，淫侈不軌，賊臣篡子滋起矣。
translations.literal: Yet upholding the righteousness of the royal house, they made punitive expeditions as lords of alliances. Politics came from the Five Hegemons, feudal lords acted wantonly, extravagant and lawless, traitorous ministers and usurping sons arose increasingly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they upheld the royal house's righteousness, conducting punitive campaigns as alliance leaders. Power flowed from the Five Hegemons, the feudal lords ran wild, and extravagance and lawlessness spread, while traitorous ministers and usurping sons multiplied.

context.previous: 是後或力政，彊乘弱，興師不請天子。
context.next: 齊、晉、秦、楚其在成周微甚，封或百里或五十里。

translations.chinese: 齊、晉、秦、楚其在成周微甚，封或百里或五十里。
translations.literal: Qi, Jin, Qin, and Chu were insignificant in the time of prosperous Zhou, their fiefs only a hundred li or fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, Jin, Qin, and Chu were utterly insignificant during Zhou's prosperous era, their fiefs no more than a hundred li or fifty li.

context.previous: 然挾王室之義，以討伐為會盟主，政由五伯，諸侯恣行，淫侈不軌，賊臣篡子滋起矣。
context.next: 晉阻三河，齊負東海，楚介江淮，秦因雍州之固，四海迭興，更為伯主，文武所褒大封，皆威而服焉。

translations.chinese: 晉阻三河，齊負東海，楚介江淮，秦因雍州之固，四海迭興，更為伯主，文武所褒大封，皆威而服焉。
translations.literal: Jin blocked the three rivers, Qi faced the eastern sea, Chu bordered the Jiang and Huai, Qin relied on the defenses of Yong province. The four seas rose in succession, replacing each other as hegemonic lords. Those praised and greatly enfeoffed by Wen and Wu all inspired awe and submission.
translations.idiomatic: Jin blocked the three great rivers, Qi faced the eastern sea, Chu bordered the Jiang and Huai rivers, Qin relied on Yong province's natural defenses. The powers of the four seas rose in succession, each replacing the others as hegemonic lords. Those whom Wen and Wu praised and greatly enfeoffed all inspired awe and obedience.

context.previous: 齊、晉、秦、楚其在成周微甚，封或百里或五十里。
context.next: 是以孔子明王道，干七十餘君，莫能用，故西觀周室，論史記舊聞，興於魯而次春秋，上記隱，下至哀之獲麟，約其辭文，去其煩重，以制義法，王道備，人事浹。

translations.chinese: 是以孔子明王道，干七十餘君，莫能用，故西觀周室，論史記舊聞，興於魯而次春秋，上記隱，下至哀之獲麟，約其辭文，去其煩重，以制義法，王道備，人事浹。
translations.literal: This is why Confucius clarified the way of kings, petitioned more than seventy rulers, but none could employ him. Therefore he observed the western Zhou court, discussed historical records and old traditions, arose in Lu and arranged the Spring and Autumn Annals, recording from Yin above to the capture of the unicorn in Ai below, condensing their wording and style, removing their tedious repetitions, to establish righteous principles. The way of kings was complete, human affairs thorough.
translations.idiomatic: This is why Confucius clarified the kingly way, seeking audience with more than seventy rulers without success. He therefore observed the western Zhou court, discussed historical records and ancient traditions, rose up in Lu and compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals—from Duke Yin above to the capture of the unicorn during Duke Ai below—condensing the language and style, removing tedious repetitions, to establish principles of righteousness. The kingly way was complete, and human affairs were thoroughly covered.

context.previous: 晉阻三河，齊負東海，楚介江淮，秦因雍州之固，四海迭興，更為伯主，文武所褒大封，皆威而服焉。
context.next: 七十子之徒口受其傳指，為有所刺譏褒諱挹損之文辭不可以書見也。

translations.chinese: 七十子之徒口受其傳指，為有所刺譏褒諱挹損之文辭不可以書見也。
translations.literal: The disciples of the seventy worthies orally received his transmitted teachings, for there were passages of criticism, mockery, praise, concealment, and depreciation in the wording that could not be shown in writing.
translations.idiomatic: The disciples of the seventy worthies received his transmitted teachings orally, for the wording contained passages of criticism, mockery, praise, concealment, and depreciation that could not be committed to writing.

context.previous: 是以孔子明王道，干七十餘君，莫能用，故西觀周室，論史記舊聞，興於魯而次春秋，上記隱，下至哀之獲麟，約其辭文，去其煩重，以制義法，王道備，人事浹。
context.next: 魯君子左丘明懼弟子人人異端，各安其意，失其真，故因孔子史記具論其語，成左氏春秋。

translations.chinese: 魯君子左丘明懼弟子人人異端，各安其意，失其真，故因孔子史記具論其語，成左氏春秋。
translations.literal: The Lu gentleman Zuoqiu Ming feared that disciples would each follow different doctrines, each comfortable with their own opinions, losing the truth, so based on Confucius's historical records he comprehensively discussed their sayings, completing the Zuo Tradition Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: The Lu gentleman Zuoqiu Ming feared that disciples would each follow different doctrines, each content with their own opinions and losing the truth, so based on Confucius's historical records he comprehensively discussed their sayings, completing the Zuo Tradition Spring and Autumn Annals.

context.previous: 七十子之徒口受其傳指，為有所刺譏褒諱挹損之文辭不可以書見也。
context.next: 鐸椒為楚威王傳，為王不能盡觀春秋，采取成敗，卒四十章，為鐸氏微。

translations.chinese: 鐸椒為楚威王傳，為王不能盡觀春秋，采取成敗，卒四十章，為鐸氏微。
translations.literal: Duo Jiao wrote a commentary for King Wei of Chu, but the king could not read the entire Spring and Autumn Annals, so he selected successes and failures, finally making forty chapters, calling it the Duo Family Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Duo Jiao wrote a commentary for King Wei of Chu, but since the king could not read the Spring and Autumn Annals in full, he selected examples of success and failure and in the end produced forty chapters called the Duo Family Annals.

context.previous: 魯君子左丘明懼弟子人人異端，各安其意，失其真，故因孔子史記具論其語，成左氏春秋。
context.next: 趙孝成王時，其相虞卿上采春秋，下觀近勢，亦著八篇，為虞氏春秋。

translations.chinese: 趙孝成王時，其相虞卿上采春秋，下觀近勢，亦著八篇，為虞氏春秋。
translations.literal: In the time of King Xiaocheng of Zhao, his chancellor Yu Qing selected from the Spring and Autumn Annals above and observed recent trends below, also writing eight chapters, calling it the Yu Family Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: During King Xiaocheng of Zhao's reign, his chancellor Yu Qing drew from the Spring and Autumn Annals above and observed recent developments below, also writing eight chapters called the Yu Family Spring and Autumn Annals.

context.previous: 鐸椒為楚威王傳，為王不能盡觀春秋，采取成敗，卒四十章，為鐸氏微。
context.next: 呂不韋者，秦莊襄王相，亦上觀尚古，刪拾春秋，集六國時事，以為八覽、六論、十二紀，為呂氏春秋。

translations.chinese: 呂不韋者，秦莊襄王相，亦上觀尚古，刪拾春秋，集六國時事，以為八覽、六論、十二紀，為呂氏春秋。
translations.literal: Lü Buwei was chancellor to King Zhuangxiang of Qin, and also looked up to revere antiquity, edited and collected from the Spring and Autumn Annals, gathered events from the time of the six states, making them into eight surveys, six discussions, and twelve records, calling it the Lü Family Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Buwei was chancellor to King Zhuangxiang of Qin, and, revering antiquity, edited and collected from the Spring and Autumn Annals, gathered events from the time of the six states, making them into eight surveys, six discussions, and twelve records, calling it the Lü Family Spring and Autumn Annals.

context.previous: 趙孝成王時，其相虞卿上采春秋，下觀近勢，亦著八篇，為虞氏春秋。
context.next: 及如荀卿、孟子、公孫固、韓非之徒，各往往捃摭春秋之文以著書，不同勝紀。

translations.chinese: 及如荀卿、孟子、公孫固、韓非之徒，各往往捃摭春秋之文以著書，不同勝紀。
translations.literal: And like Xun Qing, Mencius, Gongsun Gu, and Han Fei and their followers, each collected fragments from the Spring and Autumn Annals' text to write books, differing greatly in their accounts.
translations.idiomatic: And like Xun Qing, Mencius, Gongsun Gu, and Han Fei and their followers, each collected fragments from the Spring and Autumn Annals' text to write books, with greatly differing accounts.

context.previous: 呂不韋者，秦莊襄王相，亦上觀尚古，刪拾春秋，集六國時事，以為八覽、六論、十二紀，為呂氏春秋。
context.next: 漢相張蒼歷譜五德，上大夫董仲舒推春秋義，頗著文焉。

translations.chinese: 漢相張蒼歷譜五德，上大夫董仲舒推春秋義，頗著文焉。
translations.literal: The Han chancellor Zhang Cang calendared the five virtues, the senior grand master Dong Zhongshu expounded the Spring and Autumn Annals' principles, and wrote quite extensively about them.
translations.idiomatic: The Han chancellor Zhang Cang calendared the five virtues, and the senior grand master Dong Zhongshu expounded the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals, writing quite extensively about them.

context.previous: 及如荀卿、孟子、公孫固、韓非之徒，各往往捃摭春秋之文以著書，不同勝紀。

translations.literal: The calendar makers take their years and months, several schools exalt divine destiny, the chronological records and secret accounts only record posthumous titles, their words are concise, but to view the essentials comprehensively is difficult.

translations.literal: Therefore I have calendared the twelve feudal lords, from the Gonghe administration until Confucius, making manifest in tables the great outlines of rise and decline criticized by Spring and Autumn Annals and Discourses of the States scholars, written in this chapter as a key summary for those who study and treat ancient texts.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I have created chronological tables for the twelve feudal lords, from the Gonghe administration until Confucius, making clear in tabular form the major outlines of rise and decline as criticized by scholars of the Spring and Autumn Annals and Discourses of the States, written in this chapter as an essential summary for those studying and interpreting ancient texts.
